4. Tres inter se conuenerunt, ut primus è lucro duplum habere secundi. Fuit autem secundi collatio 24 aureorum, tertij uero 36. Nacti uero lucrum 12 aureorum, de legitima diuisione ex pacto hæsitant.

Hic primi collatio tacitè nonnihil expressa, è conuentionis lege depromenda fuerit. Cùm enim is tanto amplius quàm secundus accipere debeat: manifestum est, oportere collata ab eo in negotiationem, duplam rationem ad secundi collationem habere, siue ea pecunia, siue opera sola, siue utrisq; æstimata fuerint. Quare si pro primo 48 aureos, duplum de 24 assumas, tum additis illis, omnis hæsitatio tolletur per regulam, sic: 108 | 12 ergo

page.notes: Left-page fragments and the fraction column at the far left are cut off by the edge of the scan. The table's fraction figures are copied as printed, with the scan's small figures unclear in places. The left margin text is not part of this page's running text. The calculation lines are printed in a small mixed hand; fractions are rendered approximately. The word "tes" at the far right stands alone and may be the catchword or the continuation of "partes". The left-edge fragments ("femuns", "leriorıs", "int nos", "scilicet", "i autem", "bus de", "tulæ 2", "una") belong to the facing page and are not transcribed.
